summary: This excerpt from a fiction book (titled 'Book 11 — part 10' in the note) opens with a household discussing the arrival of Rebecca, a dark-complexioned girl expected to keep company with Emma Jane. It then introduces the Sawyer sisters of Riverboro, Miranda, Jane and Aurelia, and Aurelia's husband Mr. L. D. M. Randall, a musician and dance caller whose impractical nature left the family poor. The note begins mid-passage and ends with Mrs. Robinson's remark about Randall's marriage.
one_line: A fiction excerpt about Rebecca's arrival in a household and the Sawyer sisters of Riverboro, including musician L. D. M. Randall.
key_facts: Rebecca has come to the household in place of another arrival, and the speaker says she will be good company for Emma Jane.
The speaker doubts that Rebecca and Emma Jane will keep her for three months.
The speaker says Rebecca looks 'black as an Injun' and is 'black and kind of up-an-comin''.
The speaker notes that Lorenzo was dark complected and that Rebecca is dark complected too.
Riverboro still called Miranda, Jane and Aurelia 'the Sawyer girls' even though Miranda and Jane were between fifty and sixty when the story opens.
Aurelia, the youngest Sawyer sister, made what she called a romantic marriage, which her sisters termed 'a mighty poor speculation'.
Mr. L. D. M. Randall taught the weekly singing-school in half a dozen neighboring towns and played the violin and 'called off' at dances.
Randall was conspicuously absent from town-meetings and purely masculine gatherings at the store, tavern or bridge.
Randall's father and twin brother died when he was still a boy.
His mother named her twin sons Marquis de Lafayette and Lorenzo de Medici Randall and supported herself by making coats until her death.
Randall's mother said, 'I'm afraid the faculties was too much divided up between my twins.'
Mrs. Robinson replied that 'L. D. M. was practical enough to get the richest girl in the village.'
